practiceQuestions.q: When did the Constituent Assembly of India hold its first meeting?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly held its first meeting on December 9, 1946, with the Muslim League boycotting it. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected as the temporary president of the Assembly following the French practice.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly in December 1946?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on December 11, 1946.

practiceQuestions.q: Who served as the Constitutional Advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sir B. N. Rau was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly. He prepared the initial draft of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, which was set up on August 29, 1947, to prepare a draft of the new Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Who moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' on December 13, 1946. It laid down the fundamentals and philosophy of the constitutional structure.

practiceQuestions.q: Who acted as the Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly?
opts: H. C. Mukherjee and V. T. Krishnamachari
B. N. Rau and S. N. Mukherjee
T. T. Krishnamachari and J. B. Kripalani
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly had two Vice-Presidents: H. C. Mukherjee and V. T. Krishnamachari.

practiceQuestions.q: How many members were there in the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee consisted of 7 members: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar (Chairman), N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer, Dr. K. M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rau, and T. T. Krishnamachari.

practiceQuestions.q: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution of India was adopted, enacted, and given to themselves by the people on 26 November 1949. Some provisions came into force on this day itself.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Union Powers Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru headed the Union Powers Committee as well as the Union Constitution Committee and States Committee.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Provincial Constitution Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the Chairman of the Provincial Constitution Committee and the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the character of the Constituent Assembly change following the enactment of the Indian Independence Act of 1947?
opts: It became completely nominated by the British Crown.
It became a fully sovereign body and functioned as the first Parliament of independent India.
It was dissolved and replaced by a completely new legislative body.
It lost its power to frame the Constitution and became solely a law-making body.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 made the Constituent Assembly a fully sovereign body, free to abrogate or alter any law made by the British Parliament. It also made it a dual-purpose body: framing the Constitution and enacting ordinary laws for the country.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the system of indirect election chosen for constituting the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan?
opts: Universal adult franchise was logistically impossible and politically immature at that stage.
The British Parliament strictly prohibited any democratic elections in India.
The Muslim League demanded indirect elections to ensure communal representation.
Mahatma Gandhi insisted that only village panchayats should choose members.
practiceQuestions.sol: Direct elections based on universal adult franchise were ruled out due to the sheer size of the population, lack of administrative machinery, and widespread illiteracy at the time. Thus, members were indirectly elected by the provincial assemblies.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas headed by Sardar Patel?
opts: It functioned as a sub-committee that drafted the preamble of the Constitution.
It was the comprehensive parent committee that appointed several specialized sub-committees like the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee.
It was exclusively responsible for negotiating with the princely states.
It had the power to veto any recommendation made by Dr. Ambedkar's Drafting Committee.

The Advisory Committee was a major parent committee under Sardar Patel which contained several sub-committees, notably the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee (J.B. Kripalani) and Minorities Sub-Committee (H.C. Mukherjee).

practiceQuestions.q: In what manner did the Constituent Assembly ensure that the Constitution represented a broad-based consensus rather than majoritarian imposition?
opts: By requiring 100% unanimous agreement on every single article before voting.
Through extensive public debate, circulation of drafts, critical feedback incorporation, and decisions based on reasoned argument and consensus.
By delegating all final decision-making power exclusively to the British Viceroy.
By prohibiting non-Congress members from participating in committee meetings.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Assembly operated through detailed committee reports, public feedback, rigorous clause-by-clause debates, and strove for consensus to accommodate diverse regional, communal, and political viewpoints.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is B. N. Rau's contribution considered foundational to the working of the Constituent Assembly, despite him not being an elected member?
opts: He personally financed the entire printing of the Constitution manuscript.
He prepared the initial blueprint/draft by studying constitutions of around 60 countries, which guided the Drafting Committee.
He acted as the Speaker of the Assembly when both Prasad and Mukherjee were absent.
He held veto power over the fundamental rights provisions.
practiceQuestions.sol: As Constitutional Advisor, B. N. Rau prepared the first draft of the Constitution based on a comparative study of the constitutions of nearly 60 countries, giving a structured base for Dr. Ambedkar's committee.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the composition of the Constituent Assembly change after the partition of India under the Mountbatten Plan?
opts: The total strength of the Assembly increased to accommodate refugees.
Representatives of areas under Pakistan seceded, reducing the Assembly's membership to 299.
All British Indian province seats were abolished, leaving only princely states.
The assembly was dissolved and a new election was ordered by the British.
practiceQuestions.sol: Following the partition, the representatives of the Muslim League from the areas falling within Pakistan withdrew from the Constituent Assembly. The total strength of the Assembly was reduced from 389 to 299.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the procedural significance of the 'Objectives Resolution' adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
opts: It served as an interim constitution until 1950.
It defined the ultimate goals, moral values, and ideological parameters that guided all subsequent committee deliberations and drafting.
It established the division of powers between the Centre and States.
It was a legally binding treaty signed with the British government.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Objectives Resolution provided the philosophical bedrock and ideological vision (freedom, equality, justice, minority protection) which influenced every provision of the final Constitution and forms the core of the Preamble.

practiceQuestions.q: Why were princely states initially hesitant to join the Constituent Assembly, and how was their participation eventually managed?
opts: They wanted complete independence or accession to Pakistan; their participation was secured through negotiations by Sardar Patel and the States Committee.
They were barred by the Cabinet Mission Plan, but joined after a civil war.
They demanded separate electorates, which Nehru rejected outright.
They refused to join until universal adult suffrage was scrapped.
practiceQuestions.sol: Initially, the princely states stayed away from the Constituent Assembly. Gradually, as the States Committee (headed by Nehru) and Sardar Patel negotiated and assured them regarding autonomy and integration, their representatives joined the Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q: Which factor best explains why the Constituent Assembly took nearly 3 years to draft the Constitution?
opts: Frequent interruptions due to world wars and internal military coups.
The meticulous, clause-by-clause scrutiny of drafts, incorporation of diverse socio-political inputs, and extensive deliberations on federalism and rights.
A deliberate delay tactics employed by the British legal advisors.
The complete absence of any pre-drafted constitutional material.
practiceQuestions.sol: The assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days because every clause of the draft was subjected to rigorous, clause-by-clause debate, reflecting the magnitude of framing a constitution for a diverse, continental-sized nation.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Constituent Assembly handle the dual responsibility of constitution-making and ordinary law-making after August 15, 1947?
opts: It appointed two separate parliaments functioning in different cities.
It met as a constituent body under Dr. Rajendra Prasad and as a legislative body under G. V. Mavalankar.
It stopped making laws and outsourced legislation to the British Privy Council.
It alternated days between drafting laws and drafting the constitution under the same chairman.
practiceQuestions.sol: When the Assembly met as the Constituent body, it was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad. When it met as the Dominion Legislature (Parliament), it was chaired by G. V. Mavalankar. This continued until March 1951.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The members of the Constituent Assembly were elected directly by the people of India on the basis of universal adult franchise.
2. The seats allocated to each British province were divided among the three principal communities: Muslims, Sikhs, and General.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the members were elected indirectly by the members of the provincial assemblies, who themselves were elected on a limited franchise, not by universal adult franchise. Statement 2 is correct: seats allocated to British provinces were distributed among Muslims, Sikhs, and General (all others) in proportion to their population.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the committees of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The Steering Committee was headed by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
2. The Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by G. V. Mavalankar.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Steering Committee was headed by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, not Dr. Ambedkar (who headed the Drafting Committee). Statement 2 is correct: G. V. Mavalankar headed the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the enactment and enforcement of the Constitution:
1. The Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949, and all its provisions came into force immediately on that very day.
2. The Indian Independence Act of 1947 and the Government of India Act of 1935 were formally repealed by Article 395 of the newly enacted Constitution.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because only some provisions (like citizenship, elections, provisional parliament) came into force on November 26, 1949; the major part of the Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950. Statement 2 is correct: Article 395 repealed the Indian Independence Act and the Government of India Act, 1935.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constituent Assembly's sovereignty:
1. After the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the Constituent Assembly could make any law it pleased and amend any British parliamentary legislation concerning India.
2. The Assembly could be vetoed by the British Crown if laws passed were deemed against imperial interests.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: the 1947 Act made the Assembly a fully sovereign body with constituent and legislative powers. Statement 2 is incorrect because the British Crown's veto power was abolished; laws passed by the Assembly did not require royal assent to become effective.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the drafting process of the Constitution:
1. The Drafting Committee published its first draft of the Constitution in February 1948, inviting public comments, criticisms, and suggestions.
2. The Constituent Assembly held a total of 11 sessions spread over nearly three years to complete its work.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Drafting Committee prepared the first draft in Feb 1948 and gave people 8 months to discuss and suggest changes. The Assembly met in 11 sessions over 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the representation of sections in the Constituent Assembly:
1. Mahatma Gandhi was a member of the Constituent Assembly and actively participated in drafting the provisions.
2. All major political parties, except the Muslim League during certain phases, were represented in the Assembly, which also included prominent jurists and women members.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Mahatma Gandhi was NOT a member of the Constituent Assembly. Statement 2 is correct: the Assembly included representatives from all communities, political parties (barring the League after partition), prominent jurists like Alladi and Ambedkar, and women members like Sarojini Naidu and Durgabai Deshmukh.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the key committees and their heads:
1. Committee on Rules of Procedure: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
2. States Committee (Committee for Negotiating with States): Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Dr. Rajendra Prasad headed the Committee on Rules of Procedure. Statement 2 is incorrect because the States Committee (Committee for Negotiating with States) was headed by Jawaharlal Nehru, not Sardar Patel (Patel headed the Provincial Constitution Committee and States Reorganization/Advisory Committee).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the functioning style of the Constituent Assembly:
1. Most of the decisions in the Assembly were made through majoritarian voting without any regard for minority concerns.
2. B. Shiva Rao and other constitutional experts noted that the Assembly's debates reflected extensive cross-ideological discussions and democratic consensus-building.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Assembly actively avoided majoritarian imposition and sought consensus, especially regarding minority rights, language, and federal provisions. Statement 2 is correct; scholarly evaluations highlight the deep commitment to reasoned debate and consensus.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the symbols and legal documentation of the Constituent Assembly's work:
1. Prem Behari Narain Raizada was the calligrapher of the original Constitution of India, which was handwritten in a flowing italic style.
2. The elephant was adopted as the symbol (seal) of the Constituent Assembly.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Prem Behari Narain Raizada calligraphed the original Constitution in English, and the elephant was chosen as the official seal/symbol of the Constituent Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the final phase of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The Constituent Assembly held its final session on January 24, 1950, where it unanimously elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India.
2. After completing the constitution-making, the Assembly ceased to exist immediately and was not transformed into the Provisional Parliament.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is incorrect because Dr. Rajendra Prasad was declared President by the Assembly on Jan 24, 1950, but he was not 'elected' via a general or contested vote—he was unanimously declared/chosen. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Constituent Assembly did NOT cease to exist; it transformed itself into the Provisional Parliament of India until the first general elections in 1951-52.
